niche: a mobile game studio's weekly tracking-quality run deciding which iOS and Android builds of its puzzle game get a purchase-tracking-loss alert, judged on the share of each build's store-verified purchases whose client purchase event never reaches the warehouse, in a week when the newest build is three days into a staged rollout on a new analytics SDK that sends at once on iOS and holds batches on Android, and weekly players on old builds come back a week or two apart
answer: Alert Android 7.41.0 and iOS 7.42.0 in the run of Monday 9 November, and no other build.
stakeholder_role: data quality lead in a mobile game studio's analytics team, who runs the weekly tracking-quality check on the game's production builds

spine.entity: one session start the game's session service recorded, every phone and tablet

world.geography: Ireland (a Dublin game studio; players worldwide; personas on the en_IE index)

driver: An item missing from a source's feed is lost only once its sending device has had its next chance to send it, a chance a separate real-time log records device by device; the loss is read over the items whose device has made contact since, the few still open completed at the source's own share of resolved gaps, while a settle window counts slow senders' waiting items as lost, cannot judge a source too new to settle and swaps two new sources whose delivery changed in opposite directions, and reading the chance at the account instead of the device grants chances that never came.
driver_concrete: A purchase event the game's analytics SDK could not send before the player left the game waits on that phone until the phone next opens the game, which the session service records the moment it happens; a missing event whose phone has opened the game since is lost, and the few still open resolve at the build's own share of resolved gaps, so Android 7.41.0 loses 6.34 per cent with none open and iOS 7.42.0 on the new SDK at least 3.10 per cent, while a seven-day settle window charges the weekly players' waiting events on the 7.38, 7.39 and 7.40 builds as losses and leaves the 7.42.0 builds unjudged, and any reading by age puts Android 7.42.0, whose WorkManager uploads hold a third of its events, above iOS 7.42.0, whose 5.0.1 SDK sends at once.
stump: A competent solver counts a purchase as lost when its event is still missing seven days later, alerts Android 7.41.0 and four old builds whose weekly players have not opened the game again (Android 7.38.1, iOS 7.38.2, 7.39.1 and 7.40.0) and leaves the 7.42.0 builds unjudged for want of a week-old purchase, so iOS 7.42.0 is missed and 5 of the 12 builds are wrong; the step that lands it there is judging a missing event by its age instead of by whether the phone that made the purchase has opened the game since.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who collapses the SDK's duplicate uploads and restored events, drops pass renewals and sandbox and licence-tester purchases, maps build numbers through the register and reads the window in Irish dates, then counts a purchase as lost when its event is still missing seven days later, files 5 of the 12 builds wrong (four old builds alerted, iOS 7.42.0 missed); a fourteen-day window still misses iOS 7.42.0, a pooled arrival curve files 6 wrong, a short window for the 7.42.0 pair alerts Android 7.42.0, and the next session read by account instead of by phone files false alerts on iOS 7.38.2, 7.39.1 and 7.40.0.
domain_test: The deciding quantity is a build's purchase-tracking loss, the client-side instrumentation reconciled against the store's server-side purchases with each missing event judged against its phone's next session, the measurement work product analysts do on SDK telemetry; with wards, meters or tills for builds there is no on-device event queue, no session handshake and no store receipt, and the task stops making sense.

differentiation.task234: task234 predicts each source's eventual output from a share in its own current output that a loss cannot move; this build predicts nothing: it identifies purchase by purchase whether the missing event is due yet, from a separate real-time log of the sending phone's next session, and measures loss only over the purchases that are due
differentiation.task231: task231 takes the closed share of silent units from settled rounds the register has caught up with; this build has no settled rounds to borrow from (the newest build is four days old) and judges each missing item by its own sender's next contact, not by a share carried from earlier periods
differentiation.task445: task445 completes a still-open period by imputing each missing reporter's amount from its class's drift; this build imputes no amount: each missing item is classified late or lost by whether its own sending device has made contact since, read from a separate session log, and the loss rate is measured over the items whose device has
differentiation.task459: task459 reads each unit's rate at a committed operating level from interval records instead of its period average; this build has no operating level or rate curve: it decides, item by item, whether a missing record is due yet from its sender's next contact and measures loss only over the items that are
differentiation.task235: v1 graded each build's tracking loss at two decimals, a figure that moved with the rate given to the purchases still open at the run; v2 grades only what the records force (each build's alert, the losses known outright, iOS 7.42.0's floor) and files the outcome (an event that has not arrived by the run is lost only if it never will), and the account links now say they are not a full register of a player's accounts: the decisive step (each missing event judged against the next session of the phone that made the purchase) is unchanged and still unfiled.
differentiation.task197: task197 measures a unit's response to a shared signal over seconds when its output also runs a scheduled trajectory the records give only as endpoints; nothing here responds to a signal or follows a trajectory: an item missing from a feed is judged by whether its own device has had its next chance to send it, a chance the session log records device by device

lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-17: determinism judge SEND_BACK, underspecified_objective (the alert list graded each build's tracking loss at two decimals though nothing shipped said how the purchases still open at the run are valued, and paying players were read off the account links, which no file said were incomplete); the alert set was forced and Gate H passed

notes: v2 Decisive G12 (a missing purchase event is a non-answer until the phone that made the purchase has opened the game again), G14 supporting (the loss read over the purchases whose chance has come, the few still open at the build's own share of resolved gaps, pattern E's form), G2 (the chance belongs to the device, not the account). The metrics catalogue files the WHAT (a build's tracking loss: the share of its purchases in the four weeks whose purchase_completed event never reaches the warehouse; purchases made shortly before the run count like any other, and an event not arrived by the run is lost only if it never will; the 2 per cent line) and no method; the SDK notes say the queue is kept when the game closes and uploaded when it starts and while it is in the foreground, and that 5.0.1 sends at once on iOS and through WorkManager on Android; no sentence links a missing event to the phone's next session. The graded list carries the alert, paying players and gross bookings per paying player; no figure that moves with the rate given to the open purchases is graded (the alert set is the same under the build's own, the platform's or the pooled rate, or a silence cut-off).
